content:
Facts: Children totally excluded from mother’s will (which left entire estate to grandchildren) sought reduction without prior acceptance with benefit of inventory; co-heirs raised inadmissibility defense.
Legal Framework: Art. 564 Civil Code (benefit of inventory requirement); Art. 557 Civil Code (legitimate heirs); Art. 537 Civil Code (reserved portions).
Interpretative Issues: Whether totally pretermitted legitimate heirs must accept inheritance with benefit of inventory before bringing reduction action; distinction between pretermitted heirs and co-heirs for different inheritances of same decedent.
Legal Principles: Totally pretermitted legitimate heirs are not required to accept inheritance with benefit of inventory before bringing reduction action, as they acquire heir status only after successful reduction. This applies both in testamentary succession (when testator disposed of entire estate) and intestate succession (when deceased disposed of entire estate by donation). However, this exception applies only to the inheritance where heir is pretermitted; for other inheritances where heir is co-heir with residual assets, simple acceptance renders reduction action inadmissible without prior acceptance with benefit of inventory. ID: ITI157; Instance_Type: First instance; Legal_Duration: P6Y11M
